efile.text: Form 306 and the tax due on it must be submitted electronically if either of the following apply: the amount required to be withheld from wages paid during the previous calendar year is $1,000 or more; or the employer contracts with a third-party payroll service provider to file and remit North Dakota income tax withheld on the employer's behalf, and the provider electronically files and remits the employer's withholding taxes for federal tax purposes.

deposits.interpretation: North Dakota has no deposit schedule: Form 306 is filed and paid for each calendar quarter, on or before April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 (it must be filed even if no wages were paid). An employer may instead file and pay ANNUALLY, one Form 306 for the whole year due January 31 after the year, if it filed and paid all four quarters of the preceding year on time AND withheld less than $1,000 in the preceding year; the employer must contact the Commissioner (withhold@nd.gov) before the first quarter's return. The annual option is therefore an INPUT (assignedFrequency 'annual') and is never derived. Because a payroll service provider that files the employer's federal taxes electronically makes ND electronic filing mandatory for that employer, a payroll platform's customers should be treated as electronic filers.

lookback.description: North Dakota income tax withheld in the preceding calendar year (only used to decide electronic filing, not the schedule)

returns.name: Form 306, North Dakota Income Tax Withholding Return
contents: Filed for each calendar quarter by April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31, even if no wages were paid.
Annual filers file one Form 306 for the calendar year by January 31.
Electronic submission through TAP (ACH debit) or by ACH credit with Form 301-EF; an ACH credit satisfies the filing requirement. Paper only if not required to file electronically or with a waiver.

returns.name: Forms W-2, 1099, 1042-S and W-2G showing North Dakota withholding
contents: The state requirement is met by filing a copy of the form filed with SSA or IRS with the state information section completed; filed electronically (waiver for good cause).
Methods: Taxpayer Access Point (upload or key), or an upload web service called from accounting software (technical guidance at www.tax.nd.gov/SoftwareDevelopers).
A zero annual reconciliation is a .txt/.csv file of FEIN and year uploaded in TAP.

returns.name: Employer's Contribution and Wage Report
contents: Due April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 with the tax; a weekend or holiday moves the date to the next business day (handbook).
Liable employers file the report electronically (UI EASY) with the tax due; reports and payments not submitted electronically on time are subject to interest and penalty (agency File Reports page).
